bsb.text: Do not envy wicked men or desire their company;

explanation.text:
studieth--meditateth.

talk . . . mischief--Their expressed purposes are to do evil.

bsb.text: for their hearts devise violence, and their lips declare trouble.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 14:1; Isa 54:14).

house--including the family.

bsb.text: By wisdom a house is built and by understanding it is established;

explanation.text: by knowledge . . . riches-- (Pro 8:18; Pro 21:20).

bsb.text: through knowledge its rooms are filled with every precious and beautiful treasure.

explanation.text: The general statement (Ecc 9:16, Ecc 9:18) is specially illustrated (compare Pro 21:22; Psa 144:1).

bsb.text: A wise man is strong, and a man of knowledge enhances his strength.

explanation.text:
For by wise counsel thou shall make thy war,.... Counsel, as well as strength, is necessary for war: kings and states, before they enter on a war, should not only well consider the justness of their cause, but should consult whether they have a sufficiency of men and money to carry it on; and should concert the wisest methods to attack the enemy, or defend themselves; and, above all, should ask counsel of God; see 2 Kings 18:20. And this is true of our spiritual warfare with sin, Satan, the world, and false teachers; which requires not only strength to wage war with them, but wise counsel, that we may be able to understand and guard against their cunning, wiles, and stratagems: and this is principally to be asked of God, who is wonderful in counsel; and of good and experienced men, skilled in those matters;

and in the multitude of counsellors there is safety; to take the advice of wise counsellors, and many of them, even among men, is safe for princes and states, in the above case and in all others; and especially to ask and take counsel of God, who gives wisdom liberally to them that ask it; and of Christ, the wonderful Counsellor; and from the Scriptures, whom David made his counsellors; and from old experienced Christians, and ministers of the word, with whom are wisdom, counsel, and understanding; See Gill on Proverbs 11:14.

bsb.text: Only with sound guidance should you wage war, and victory lies in a multitude of counselors.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 14:16).

in the gate--(Compare Pro 22:22).

bsb.text: Wisdom is too high for a fool; he does not open his mouth in the meeting place.

explanation.text: So called even if he fails to do evil.

bsb.text: He who plots evil will be called a schemer.

explanation.text: Same thought varied.

bsb.text: A foolish scheme is sin, and a mocker is detestable to men.

explanation.text: Literally, "If thou fail in the day of straits (adversity), strait (or, small) is thy strength," which is then truly tested.

bsb.text: If you faint in the day of distress, how small is your strength!

explanation.text:
Neglect of known duty is sin (Jam 4:17).

ready--literally, "bowing down"

to be slain--that is, unjustly. God's retributive justice cannot be avoided by professed ignorance.

bsb.text: Rescue those being led away to death, and restrain those stumbling toward the slaughter.
If you say, “Behold, we did not know about this,” does not He who weighs hearts consider it? Does not the One who guards your life know? Will He not repay a man according to his deeds?

explanation.text: As delicious food whets the appetite, so should the rewards of wisdom excite us to seek it.

bsb.text: Eat honey, my son, for it is good, and the honeycomb is sweet to your taste.

explanation.text: reward--literally, "after part," the proper result (compare Pro 23:18; Psa 37:37-38).

bsb.text: Know therefore that wisdom is sweet to your soul. If you find it, there is a future for you, and your hope will never be cut off.

explanation.text: The plots of the wicked against the good, though partially, shall not be fully successful (Psa 37:24); while the wicked, falling under penal evil, find no help.

bsb.text: Do not lie in wait, O wicked man, near the dwelling of the righteous; do not destroy his resting place.

explanation.text: seven times--often, or many (Pro 6:16, Pro 6:31; Pro 9:1).

bsb.text: For though a righteous man may fall seven times, he still gets up; but the wicked stumble in bad times.

explanation.text: Yet let none rejoice over the fate of evildoers, lest God punish their wrong spirit by relieving the sufferer (compare Pro 17:5; Job 31:29).

bsb.text: Do not gloat when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart rejoice when he stumbles,

explanation.text:
Lest the Lord see it, and it displease him,.... Who sees all things, not only external actions, but the heart, and the inward motions of it; and though men may hide the pleasure they feel at the misery of an enemy from others, they cannot hide it from the Lord; nor is this said by way of doubt, but as a certain thing; and which the Lord not barely sees, but takes notice of, and to such a degree as to resent it, and show his displeasure at it by taking the following step;

and he turn away his wrath from him; remove the effects of it, raise him out of his fallen and distressed condition, and restore him to his former prosperous one; and not only so, but turn it upon thee, as Gersom supplies the words, and not amiss; so that there is a strange and sudden change of circumstances; thou that was pleasing thyself with the distress of thine enemy art fallen into the same, and he is delivered out of it; which must be a double affliction to such a man; so that by rejoicing at an enemy, he is doing his enemy good and himself hurt; see Proverbs 17:5.

bsb.text: or the LORD will see and disapprove, and turn His wrath away from him.
Do not fret over evildoers, and do not be envious of the wicked.

explanation.text: candle--or, "prosperity"; it shall come to an end (Pro 13:9; Pro 20:20).

bsb.text: For the evil man has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.

explanation.text:
A warning against impiety and resistance to lawful rule (Rom 13:1-7; Pe1 2:17).

meddle . . . change--(Compare Margin), literally, "mingle not yourself," avoid the society of restless persons.

bsb.text: My son, fear the LORD and the king, and do not associate with the rebellious.

explanation.text: their calamity, etc.--either what God and the king inflict, or what changers and their company suffer; better the first.

bsb.text: For they will bring sudden destruction. Who knows what ruin they can bring?

explanation.text:
These . . . wise--literally, "are of the wise," as authors (compare "Psalms of David," Hebrew). "These" refers to the verses following, Pro 24:24-34.

to have respect--literally, "to discern faces," show partiality,

bsb.text: These also are sayings of the wise: To show partiality in judgment is not good.

explanation.text: of which an example is justifying the wicked, to which is opposed, rebuking him, which has a blessing.

bsb.text: Whoever tells the guilty, “You are innocent”—peoples will curse him, and nations will denounce him;

explanation.text:
But to them that rebuke him shall be delight,.... That is, such that rebuke in the gate, or openly, in a court of judicature; that reprove delinquents, such as are found guilty of malpractices, and punish them as they ought to be, according to the laws of God and man; they shall have delight in themselves, peace and pleasure in their own minds; or the people shall delight in them, and speak well of them, and think themselves happy under such a just administration; or the Lord shall delight in them, the beauty or sweetness of the Lord shall come unto them, as Aben Ezra explains it; the Lord shall be sweet and delightful to them, and they shall have pleasure in him;

and a good blessing shall come upon them; or "a blessing of good"; a blessing of good things, temporal and spiritual, here and hereafter; the blessing of a good God, and a blessing from him; and a blessing of good men, as opposed to the curse of the people in Proverbs 24:24.

bsb.text: but it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and rich blessing will come upon them.

explanation.text:
kiss his lips--love and obey, do homage (Psa 2:12; Sol 8:1).

right answer--literally, "plain words" (compare Pro 8:9), opposed to deceptive, or obscure.

bsb.text: An honest answer given is like a kiss on the lips.

explanation.text: Prepare . . . in the field--Secure, by diligence, a proper support, and then build; provide necessaries, then comforts, to which a house rather pertained, in a mild climate, permitting the use of tents.

bsb.text: Complete your outdoor work and prepare your field; after that, you may build your house.

explanation.text: Do not speak even truth needlessly against any, and never falsehood.

bsb.text: Do not testify against your neighbor without cause, and do not deceive with your lips.

explanation.text: Especially avoid retaliation (Mat 5:43-45; Rom 12:17).

bsb.text: Do not say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his work.”

explanation.text: A striking picture of the effects of sloth.

bsb.text: I went past the field of a slacker and by the vineyard of a man lacking judgment.
Thorns had grown up everywhere, thistles had covered the ground, and the stone wall was broken down.

explanation.text:
From the folly of the sluggard learn wisdom (Pro 6:10-11).

Next: Proverbs Chapter 25

bsb.text: I observed and took it to heart; I looked and received instruction:

explanation.text:
Yet a little sleep, a little slumber,.... The sight of the field and vineyard of the slothful put Solomon in mind of an observation he had made before, which fitly describes the disposition and gesture of the sluggard, by which means his field and vineyard came to ruin; while he should be up and tilling his field and planting his vineyard, he is in his bed; and awaking, instead of rising, craves for and indulges himself in another little doze, and which he repeats again and again;

a little folding of the hands to sleep; which ought to have been employed another way; See Gill on Proverbs 6:10.

bsb.text: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,

explanation.text:
So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth,.... Swiftly and suddenly, both in a temporal and spiritual sense; See Gill on Proverbs 6:11;

and thy want as an armed man; irresistibly. Here ends according to some the "second", according to others the "third" part of this book of Proverbs, another beginning with the following chapter.

bsb.text: and poverty will come upon you like a robber, and need like a bandit.
